confidentUnsupported.evidence: Heading 'Likely cause: float switch' is hedged and offers an alternative ('or the control board'), so not a definitive claim, but it is weakly supported.

rationale: The assistant correctly covered container seating but then fixated on a float inside the container and never directed the customer to the key owner check for a Bosch condenser: cleaning the container sieve and the hidden pump sump compartment behind the small cover, which the ground truth shows would have improved the fault. It skipped useful questions (how far into the cycle it stops, smells, drain hose kit) and jumped to 'the water level switch or the control board is faulty' and an engineer after only three exchanges. The engineer referral is an acceptable end point given the stacked unit, but it was premature and left a likely free fix untried; no parts were pushed and nothing was invented, though the premature 'suitable replacement' model panel was out of place.
